RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference number: POC-E71C638D4F-57015
Member: Taylor Grant (ID W785887548)
Requested service: Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-06
Appeal deadline: 2027-02-02

To the Appeals & Grievances Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130) for Taylor Grant, communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-06. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in the notice (by 2027-02-02).

Based on my research, Harvard Pilgrim delegates prior authorization and medical necessity review for hip replacement surgery (including CPT 27130) to its vendor, Evolent, and the applicable clinical criteria are set out in "Evolent Clinical Guideline 1761 for Hip Arthroplasty" (Evolent_CG_1761). I was able to obtain and review the text of that guideline. I have not been able to independently confirm that the copy I reviewed is word-for-word identical to whatever version/edition of Evolent_CG_1761 was applied to this specific request on 2026-08-06; I am therefore also formally requesting, below, that the plan confirm the exact policy version used and provide it in writing. Everything placed in quotation marks below is text I actually retrieved from Evolent_CG_1761; everything else is my own summary or argument.

The clinical record supports approval under this guideline for the following reasons:

1. Duration and functional impact of symptoms
The guideline's Total Hip Arthroplasty "Section Two" pathway requires: "There is persistent pain and documented loss of function for at least 12 weeks." Mr./Ms. Grant has had 9 months (approximately 39 weeks) of progressive hip pain unrelieved by rest — well beyond the 12-week threshold. Functional loss is documented and severe: the patient ambulates with a cane, is limited to walking one block, and cannot put on shoes unassisted. This directly satisfies the guideline's general requirement of "[h]ip pain with documented loss of function, which may include painful weight bearing, painful or inadequate range of motion to accomplish age-appropriate activities of daily living (ADLs) and/or employment, and mechanical catching, locking."

2. Physical examination findings
The guideline requires that "[p]hysical exam demonstrates findings of hip pathology as evidenced by one or more of the following: Painful, limited range of motion or antalgic gait; Contracture; Crepitus; Leg length difference." The exam documented positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, satisfying this element.

3. Radiographic findings — directly addressing the stated denial reason
The denial states that the submitted imaging findings do not support medical necessity. The guideline specifies that qualifying radiographic evidence includes: "Radiographic findings show evidence of advanced arthritic changes, described as Tönnis grade 2 or 3 or described as X-rays showing advanced changes (e.g., severe narrowing, bone-on-bone compartment collapse, subchondral sclerosis or cysts, osteophyte formation and/or bony deformity etc.)" and that "X-rays described only as showing 'severe', 'advanced' or 'end-stage' arthritis require more definitive descriptions as stated above (weightbearing X-rays are not required)."

The weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph obtained on 2026-05-28 provides exactly this level of definitive description: joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes. This is a weight-bearing film (exceeding what the guideline requires) showing near-complete joint space loss, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophyte formation — the specific findings the guideline lists as qualifying evidence of advanced disease. I am unable to state a formal Tönnis grade because the radiology report provided does not assign one; however, the descriptive findings independently satisfy the guideline's alternative "described as X-rays showing advanced changes" standard. If the plan's reviewer requires a formal Tönnis grade, I ask that Dr. Duval be given the opportunity to supply one or to peer-review the actual films, consistent with the plan's peer-to-peer process.

4. Failed non-operative treatment
The guideline requires "[f]ailure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least two of the following: Rest or inactivity modifications/limitations; Weight reduction for individual with elevated BMI; Protected weight-bearing with cane, walker, or crutches; Physical therapy modalities; Physician supervised exercise program (including home exercise program); Pharmacological treatment: oral/topical NSAIDs, acetaminophen, or analgesics; Intra-articular corticosteroid injection." The record documents three qualifying modalities over far more than 12 weeks:
- Supervised physical therapy targeting hip abductor strengthening and gait, 16 weeks, 2026-02-19 through 2026-06-11 (20 visits completed, per the PT discharge note);
- NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief; and
- An intra-articular corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-26, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.

5. Absence of contraindications
The guideline lists as an absolute contraindication "[a]ny corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery." The injection in this record was given on 2026-03-26. As of the date of this appeal, more than 12 weeks have elapsed since that injection, and I ask the plan to confirm with Dr. Duval's office the anticipated surgical date to verify this interval is met at the time of surgery. The record also documents no active local or systemic infection, no untreated substance dependency, and a BMI of 29 (well under the guideline's relative-contraindication threshold of "BMI > 40kg/m2"), and the patient is a non-smoker. [Documentation of dental/oral hygiene status was not included in the packet I reviewed; Dr. Duval's office can supply this if the plan requires it to complete the General Requirements review.]

6. Requesting surgeon
This request is submitted by Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery, who can be reached to provide any additional clarifying documentation or to participate in a peer-to-peer review.

Requested action
Based on the above, the clinical record satisfies the medical necessity criteria in Evolent Clinical Guideline 1761 for Hip Arthroplasty for Total Hip Arthroplasty (CPT 27130). I ask that the denial be reversed and the requested procedure approved. In the alternative, I ask that the plan:
(a) identify the specific edition/date of Evolent_CG_1761 applied to this request and provide it to me and to Dr. Duval in writing;
(b) specify which particular element of the criteria the reviewer found unmet by the imaging, since the weight-bearing radiograph appears to meet the guideline's stated descriptive standard; and
(c) offer a peer-to-peer review between Dr. Duval and the reviewing physician before this appeal is decided.

Enclosed with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-02-19 to 2026-06-11)
- Medication/treatment history documenting 8 months of NSAID use and the 2026-03-26 corticosteroid injection
- Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph and radiology report dated 2026-05-28
- Office notes documenting functional limitations and physical exam findings
- [Any additional surgeon narrative letter, if provided]
